source_open_excerpt:
, we propose the following two conjectures.

	If a cubic graph admits a $2$-homogeneous coloring,
	then $4$ colors are always sufficient.
target: Prove that for every finite simple cubic graph G: if there is a proper vertex coloring c using any finite color set such that exactly two distinct colors occur in the open neighborhood of every vertex, then there is such a proper coloring c' using at most four colors; or give one explicit finite simple cubic graph, rigorously verify that it has some 2-homogeneous proper coloring, and prove that no such coloring using at most four colors exists.
title: Four colors for 2-homogeneous cubic-graph colorings
